edges.effect_quant: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: This factor likely influences Falls through a mix of reserve, disability, social engagement, inflammation, and shared chronic-disease burden rather than one single biochemical pathway. That matters because some of these variables behave partly as markers of physiologic aging and partly as modifiable contributors.
edges.summary: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts link thoracic kyphosis to higher risk of falls in older adults. The average effect is usually small rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
